손님.x: Some guests are coming to my house this evening.
손님.e: 손 (old word for guest) + 님 (honorific) — not related to 손 'hand'.

숟가락.e: 술 (spoonful) + 가락 (thin stick); ㄹ became ㄷ.
숟가락.t: Pronounced [숟까락]. Spelling trap: ㄷ in 숟가락 but ㅅ in 젓가락.

비누.ex: 밥 먹기 전에 비누로 손을 씻으세요.
비누.x: Wash your hands with soap before eating.

들다.forms: 들어요 · 들었어요 · 들 거예요 · 드세요 (ㄹ drops)
들다.m: to hold, to carry (in the hand); to lift
들다.ex: 이 가방이 무거워요. 같이 들어 주세요.
들다.x: This bag is heavy. Please carry it with me.
들다.e: Watch out: other 들다 mean 'enter' (as in 들어가다) and 'cost' (돈이 들다).
들다.t: Careful: 들어요 can also come from 듣다 'listen', and 드세요 can mean 'please eat' (드시다).

배달하다.ex: 피자 한 판을 집으로 배달해 주세요.
배달하다.x: Please deliver one pizza to my house.
배달하다.e: Literally 'hand out until it reaches' the customer.
배달하다.t: To order delivery food, Koreans often say 시켜 먹다: "치킨 시켜 먹을까요?"

사고가 나다.forms: 사고가 나요 · 사고가 났어요 · 사고가 날 뻔했어요
사고가 나다.m: an accident happens, to have an accident
사고가 나다.ex: 눈이 많이 와서 도로에서 사고가 났어요.
사고가 나다.x: It snowed a lot, so there was an accident on the road.
사고가 나다.e: Literally 'an accident comes out'; 나다 is used for events like 불이 나다 'a fire breaks out'.

주사.x: The child was scared of the shot and cried a lot.
주사.e: Literally 'pour and shoot': liquid shot into the body.
주사.t: Careful: 주사가 있다 can mean 'gets nasty when drunk', which is a different word.

스키.ex: 겨울 방학에 가족들과 스키를 타러 갔어요.
스키.x: During winter break, I went skiing with my family.
스키.t: Skiing uses 타다 'to ride': 스키를 타다, just like 자전거를 타다.

관광객.ex: 명동에는 주말마다 외국인 관광객이 정말 많아요.
관광객.x: Myeongdong is packed with foreign tourists every weekend.

안내하다.m: to guide, to show (someone) around; to inform
안내하다.x: A staff member kindly showed us to our room.
안내하다.t: Staff say 안내해 드릴게요 'Let me show you,' using humble 드리다 when helping customers.

파일.x: I'll send you the report file by email.
파일.e: From English 'file'; Korean has no 'f', so it becomes ㅍ.

선물하다.ex: 어머니 생신에 예쁜 목도리를 하나 선물했어요.
선물하다.x: I gave my mother a pretty scarf for her birthday.

아주머니.x: The lady at the restaurant gave us more side dishes.
아주머니.e: Polite address for a married or middle-aged woman; 아줌마 is the casual version.

비교하다.x: Try comparing the prices at the two stores.
비교하다.e: Two syllables that both mean 'compare', side by side.

완전.forms: 완전 + adjective/verb: 완전 좋아요 · standard adverb: 완전히
완전.x: The movie I saw yesterday was so much fun.
완전.e: Literally 'complete and whole'; as a noun it means 'completeness'.
완전.t: Putting 완전 straight before an adjective is casual, youthful speech. In writing, use 완전히 or 아주.

환기.ex: 요리한 후에는 창문을 열고 환기를 하세요.
환기.x: After cooking, open the windows and air out the room.

조사하다.m: to investigate, to look into, to research
조사하다.ex: 숙제 때문에 한국의 전통 음식에 대해 조사했어요.
조사하다.x: I researched traditional Korean food for my homework.

기여하다.x: He contributed greatly to the company's growth.
기여하다.t: It takes 에: N에 기여하다 'to contribute to N'.

대표하다.x: Kimchi is a food that represents Korea.

인쇄하다.ex: 회의 자료를 열 장 인쇄해 주세요.
인쇄하다.x: Please print ten copies of the meeting materials.
인쇄하다.e: Literally 'stamp and brush' ink onto paper.
인쇄하다.t: For printing from a computer, people also say 출력하다 or 뽑다.

이체.x: Doing account transfers on your phone is convenient.
이체.e: Literally 'move and swap over' from one account to another.

연인.ex: 공원에서 연인들이 손을 잡고 걷고 있어요.
연인.x: Couples are walking hand in hand in the park.
연인.t: 연인 sounds a bit literary; in conversation people usually say 애인 or 남자 친구 / 여자 친구.

우선순위.ex: 바쁠 때는 일의 우선순위를 먼저 정하세요.
우선순위.x: When you're busy, decide your priorities first.
우선순위.e: 우선 'first of all' + 순위 'ranking' = ranking of what comes first.

알림.ex: 단톡방 알림이 계속 와서 꺼 놨어요.
알림.x: Group chat notifications kept coming, so I turned them off.
알림.e: Native noun from 알리다 'to let know'.
알림.t: Turn on/off notifications is 알림을 켜다/끄다. Don't confuse with 알람 'alarm (clock)'.

앞머리.x: My bangs were poking my eyes, so I trimmed them a little.
앞머리.t: Pronounced [암머리]: ㅍ turns into ㅁ before ㅁ. To get bangs is 앞머리를 내다; to grow them out is 앞머리를 기르다.

기념사진.x: After the graduation ceremony, I took a commemorative photo with my family.
기념사진.t: Used for any photo marking an occasion or a visit. To ask a passer-by: 사진 좀 찍어 주시겠어요?

튜브.x: The child played in the sea on a swim ring.
튜브.e: From English 'tube'. Konglish: in Korea it usually means an inflatable swim ring.
튜브.t: Floating on one is 튜브를 타다, literally 'to ride a tube'.

깔깔.ex: 친구들이 재미있는 영상을 보며 깔깔 웃었어요.
깔깔.x: My friends were cackling with laughter while watching a funny video.
깔깔.e: 의성어 (sound word) for high, loud laughter, often of children or girls. Its dark-vowel partner 껄껄 is a deep, hearty laugh.
깔깔.t: Verb: 깔깔거리다 or 깔깔대다 'to laugh loudly, cackle'.

보글보글.x: The kimchi stew is bubbling in the pot.
보글보글.e: Both 의성어 and 의태어: the sound and look of a small amount of liquid bubbling. Its dark-vowel partner 부글부글 is a bigger, heavier boil, and also describes seething anger.

사표.x: He handed his resignation letter to his manager yesterday.
사표.t: The fixed phrase is 사표를 내다 (to hand in one's resignation).

후임.ex: 제 후임이 오면 일을 잘 가르쳐 줄게요.
후임.x: When my successor comes, I'll teach them the job well.

저금.x: I put half of my allowance into savings.

관절.x: As you get older, your knee joints get weaker.
관절.e: Literally 'gate and node' — the hinge points where bones meet.

재활.ex: 다리 수술 후에 몇 달 동안 재활 치료를 받았어요.
재활.x: After leg surgery, I did rehab therapy for several months.

부품.ex: 이 부품은 해외에서 주문해야 해서 오래 걸려요.
부품.x: This part has to be ordered from overseas, so it takes a long time.

폐수.x: The river water got dirty because of factory wastewater.

허무하다.ex: 한 골 차이로 지니까 너무 허무했어요.
허무하다.x: Losing by just one goal felt so pointless.

부끄러움.ex: 그 아이는 부끄러움이 많아서 말을 잘 안 해요.
부끄러움.x: That child is very shy, so she doesn't talk much.

온화하다.x: That person has a gentle voice that's nice to listen to.

교만하다.ex: 교만한 사람은 다른 사람의 말을 잘 듣지 않아요.
교만하다.x: Arrogant people don't listen well to others.
교만하다.t: More literary than 거만하다; common in proverbs, sermons and moral lessons.

말수.x: He's been talking a lot less lately.
말수.e: Native 말 'words' plus 수 'number' — literally 'word count.'
말수.t: Pronounced [말쑤]; usually in 말수가 적다 (quiet) or 말수가 많다 (talkative).

단지.x: I only wanted to help, that's all.
단지.e: Both syllables mean 'only', doubled for emphasis.
단지.t: Usually ends with 뿐이다; homonym 단지 also means 'housing complex' (아파트 단지).

유비무환.m: better safe than sorry; preparation prevents trouble
유비무환.ex: 유비무환이라고, 비가 올 수도 있으니까 우산을 챙겨 가세요.
유비무환.x: Better safe than sorry—it might rain, so take an umbrella.
rel: closing the barn door too late

취지.ex: 이 행사의 취지는 어려운 이웃을 돕는 것입니다.
취지.x: The purpose of this event is to help neighbors in need.
취지.e: Literally 'aim and meaning': the point behind something.

숙박비.x: In peak season, lodging costs double.
숙박비.t: Nights are counted with 박: 2박 3일 means 'three days, two nights.'

솔솔.ex: 창문을 여니까 시원한 바람이 솔솔 불어요.
솔솔.x: When I opened the window, a cool breeze came gently blowing in.
솔솔.e: 의태어 (manner word) for something light flowing out softly and steadily. Its dark-vowel pair 술술 now mostly means 'smoothly, fluently'.
솔솔.t: Also for smells and sleepiness: 고소한 냄새가 솔솔 나요 'a nutty smell wafts'; 잠이 솔솔 와요 'I'm getting drowsy'.

뒤뚱뒤뚱.x: The penguins are waddling across the ice.
뒤뚱뒤뚱.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a heavy body rocking from side to side as it walks.
뒤뚱뒤뚱.t: The verb 뒤뚱거리다 is common: 오리가 뒤뚱거리며 걸어요. Classic for ducks, penguins and toddlers.

아장아장.x: The baby is toddling over to Mom.
아장아장.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a small child taking short, careful steps.
아장아장.t: It sounds cute and affectionate, so it isn't used for adults; for an unsteady adult, 비틀비틀 fits better.

벌컥벌컥.x: I was thirsty, so I gulped the water down.
벌컥벌컥.e: Both 의성어 and 의태어: the glugging sound and the manner of drinking a lot in big gulps.
벌컥벌컥.t: Pronounced [벌컥뻘컥]: the ㄱ batchim makes the next ㅂ tense. Single 벌컥 also means 'abruptly': 화를 벌컥 내다 'to flare up'.

매끈매끈.x: The stones on the beach are worn smooth by the waves.
매끈매끈.e: 의태어 (manner word) for a surface with nothing rough on it. Its dark-vowel pair 미끈미끈 feels slipperier.
매끈매끈.t: Common in skincare ads: 피부가 매끈매끈해져요. The shorter 매끈하다 also means 'sleek', as in a design.

뇌물.ex: 그 공무원은 뇌물을 받은 혐의로 체포되었습니다.
뇌물.x: That official was arrested on charges of taking bribes.
뇌물.t: Collocations: 뇌물을 주다 (give a bribe) and 뇌물을 받다 (take a bribe).

혐의.ex: 그는 뇌물을 받은 혐의로 조사를 받았어요.
혐의.x: He was investigated on suspicion of taking bribes.
혐의.t: Pronounced [혀믜], commonly [혀미]; pattern: ~ 혐의로 (on charges of ~).

전후.x: Postwar Korea was a very poor country.
전후.t: Homonym: 전후 (前後) means 'before and after' or 'around': 서른 전후 'around thirty'.

전후.m: before and after; context, the whole story; (with numbers) around, about
전후.ex: 사건의 전후 사정을 자세히 설명해 주세요.
전후.x: Please explain the whole background of the incident in detail.
전후.e: Literally 'front and back' — what came before and after.
전후.t: After a number it means 'about': 30세 전후 'around 30 years old'; native equivalent is 앞뒤.

우호.ex: 양국은 수교 이후 오랫동안 우호 관계를 유지해 왔습니다.
우호.x: The two countries have maintained friendly relations for a long time since establishing ties.

산문.ex: 그는 시뿐만 아니라 산문도 많이 썼어요.
산문.x: He wrote not only poetry but also a lot of prose.
산문.e: Literally 'loose writing', text not bound by meter.

변천하다.m: to change over time, to undergo transition
변천하다.ex: 이 박물관에서는 한국 의복이 변천해 온 과정을 볼 수 있어요.
변천하다.x: At this museum, you can see how Korean clothing has changed over time.
변천하다.e: Literally 'change and shift' — gradual change across history.

그럭저럭.m: so-so, more or less, somehow (getting by)
그럭저럭.x: I'm getting along okay these days.
그럭저럭.e: Rhyming pair like 이럭저럭: roughly 'this way and that'.
그럭저럭.t: Classic reply to 어떻게 지내요?: 그럭저럭 지내요 'I'm getting by.'

도토리 키 재기.forms: 도토리 키 재기다 · 도토리 키 재기 같다
도토리 키 재기.m: much of a muchness; all equally mediocre, so comparing is pointless
도토리 키 재기.ex: 두 후보의 실력은 도토리 키 재기라서 누가 이길지 몰라요.
도토리 키 재기.x: The two candidates are equally mediocre, so there's no telling who'll win.
도토리 키 재기.e: Acorns measuring their heights: they're all tiny, so the contest is pointless.

날개를 달다.forms: 날개를 달아요 · 달았어요 · 달 거예요 (ㄹ drops); often 날개를 단 듯 팔리다
날개를 달다.m: to take off, to gain momentum; to get a big boost
날개를 달다.ex: 그 드라마가 인기를 얻으면서 원작 소설도 날개를 달았어요.
날개를 달다.x: As the drama became popular, the original novel took off too.
날개를 달다.e: Literally 'to attach wings' — something suddenly able to fly.
날개를 달다.t: 날개 돋친 듯 팔리다 'to sell as if it grew wings' is the go-to phrase for something selling fast.

위계.ex: 그 회사는 위계 질서가 매우 엄격해요.
위계.x: That company has a very strict hierarchy.
위계.e: Literally 'rank and steps' — positions stacked like stairs.
위계.t: Homonym: 위계(僞計) means 'deceptive scheme', as in the legal term 위계에 의한 업무방해.

비전.m: vision (for the future); prospects, future potential
비전.ex: 이 회사는 비전이 있어서 꼭 들어가고 싶어요.
비전.x: This company has a bright future, so I really want to join it.
비전.e: From English 'vision'; Konglish twist: 비전이 있다 means 'has good prospects'.
비전.t: For eyesight, use 시력, not 비전.

차관.ex: 오늘 회의에는 장관 대신 차관이 참석했어요.
차관.x: The vice minister attended today's meeting in place of the minister.
차관.e: Literally 'next official': the one right below the minister.
차관.t: Homonym 차관 can also mean a foreign loan between governments.

매매.m: buying and selling, trade, sale (especially of real estate)
매매.ex: 이 집은 전세가 아니라 매매로 나왔어요.
매매.x: This house is on the market for sale, not for a lump-sum lease.
매매.e: Two hanja read 매: 'sell' and 'buy' — so literally 'selling and buying'.

일용직.ex: 그는 건설 현장에서 일용직으로 일하고 있어요.
일용직.x: He works as a day laborer at construction sites.
일용직.t: Pronounced [이룡직] — the ㄹ links over into the next syllable.

저학력.m: low level of education, poorly educated
저학력.ex: 저학력 때문에 취업이 어려운 사람들도 있어요.
저학력.x: Some people have trouble finding jobs because of their low education level.

일파만파.m: snowballing, spreading in ever-widening ripples (of a scandal or issue)
일파만파.ex: 그 거짓말 때문에 논란이 일파만파로 번졌어요.
일파만파.x: Because of that lie, the controversy snowballed.
일파만파.e: Literally 'one wave becomes ten thousand waves'.
일파만파.t: A news word: 사건/논란/의혹이 일파만파로 번지다 or 일파만파 확산되다.

감치.ex: 법정에서 소란을 피운 남성이 감치 처분을 받았습니다.
감치.x: A man who caused a disturbance in the courtroom was ordered into detention for contempt.
감치.e: Literally 'place under supervision'; a judge can order it for up to 20 days.
감치.t: Also used for people who refuse to pay child support or ignore court orders: 감치 명령.

관료주의.ex: 관료주의 때문에 간단한 일도 처리가 늦어져요.
관료주의.x: Because of red tape, even simple matters take a long time.
관료주의.t: Pronounced [괄료주의] — the ㄴ becomes ㄹ before ㄹ.

고위공직자.m: high-ranking public official, senior government official
고위공직자.x: Senior public officials must disclose their assets every year.
고위공직자.e: Literally 'person in a high-ranking public post'.
고위공직자.t: Often heard in the news with 공수처, the agency investigating crimes by senior officials.

결과주의.ex: 결과주의에 따르면 행위의 옳고 그름은 결과로 결정돼요.
결과주의.x: According to consequentialism, whether an act is right or wrong is decided by its results.
결과주의.e: Literally 'result-ism'; 결과 pictures a tree bearing fruit.

전도.ex: 길거리에서 전도하는 사람들을 자주 볼 수 있어요.
전도.x: You can often see people evangelizing on the street.
전도.e: Literally 'passing on the Way'; homonyms mean 'conduction' and 'tumbling over'.
전도.t: 전도하다 usually means street or door-to-door evangelism, which is very visible in Korea.

대금.ex: 대금 연주를 들으면 바람 소리가 떠올라요.
대금.x: Listening to the daegeum reminds me of the sound of the wind.
대금.e: Literally 'big flute'. Homonym alert: 대금 also means 'payment, price'.

명실상부.m: being true to the name, living up to one's title in reality
명실상부.x: He is truly Korea's best pianist, in name and in fact.
명실상부.e: Literally 'name and reality match each other'.
명실상부.t: Almost always used as 명실상부한 + noun, meaning 'undisputed, true'.

이내.ex: 아이는 한참 울다가 이내 잠이 들었어요.
이내.x: The child cried for a while and soon fell asleep.
이내.e: Homonym warning: the noun 이내 means 'within' (일주일 이내 'within a week').

일인가구.ex: 요즘 일인가구를 위한 소포장 식품이 인기예요.
일인가구.x: These days, small-package foods for single-person households are popular.
일인가구.e: Literally 'one-person household'; 가구 is the unit for counting households.
일인가구.t: Usually written 1인 가구; pronounced [이린가구] with the ㄹ linking over.

지난하다.ex: 협상은 지난한 과정을 거쳐 마침내 타결되었습니다.
지난하다.x: After an arduous process, the negotiations were finally concluded.
지난하다.t: Unrelated to 지난 'last, past' (지난주); it is formal and mostly written.

기호지세.m: a situation you can't back out of once started
기호지세.ex: 일을 이미 시작했으니 기호지세로 끝까지 가야 합니다.
기호지세.x: We've already started, so like riding a tiger, we must see it through.
기호지세.e: Literally 'the situation of riding a tiger': getting off means being eaten.

불원천리.m: going a long way gladly, not minding the distance
불원천리.x: He came all the way to his friend's wedding, not minding the distance.
불원천리.e: Literally 'not considering a thousand li far'.

쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.forms: 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다고 · 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있겠지요
쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.m: every dog has its day; good times will come eventually (lit. even a mouse hole will get sunshine one day)
쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.ex: 쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다고, 힘내면 좋은 날이 꼭 올 거예요.
쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.x: Every dog has its day, so hang in there; good days will surely come.
쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.e: Even a dark mouse hole will one day catch a ray of sunshine (볕).
쥐구멍에도 볕 들 날 있다.t: Pronounced [쥐구멍에도 볃 뜰 날 읻따]. Words of comfort after a long run of bad luck. Not to be confused with 쥐구멍에라도 숨고 싶다 'I want to crawl into a hole (from embarrassment)'.
